title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 232
paragraphs: We dismiss, then, the opinion of the Ionians, and offer a judgment of our own on this matter: that Egypt is all that land inhabited by Egyptians, just as Cilicia is the land inhabited by Cilicians and Assyria the land inhabited by Assyrians, and we know of no boundary properly speaking between Asia and Libya except the borders of Egypt. If, however, we adopt the view commonly held by the Hellenes, we shall suppose that the whole of Egypt, beginning from the Cataract and the city of Elephantine, is divided into two parts and thus partakes of both names, one side belonging to Libya and the other to Asia. For the Nile from the Cataract onwards flows to the sea, cutting Egypt through the middle; and as far as the city of Cercasorus the Nile flows in one single stream, but from this city onwards it divides into three channels. One, which is called the Pelusian mouth, turns towards the east; the second goes towards the west, and this is called the Canobic mouth; while the channel that runs straight on comes, as the river descends, to the point of the Delta, then cuts the Delta through its middle and so issues into the sea. In this channel we have a portion of the river's water that is neither the smallest nor the least famous — it is called the Sebennytic mouth. There are also two other mouths which branch off from the Sebennytic and go to the sea, called the Saïtic and the Mendesian mouth. The Bolbitinic and Bucolic mouths, on the other hand, are not natural but made by digging.
